target_customer: Renewable energy owners, utilities and infrastructure operators that need inspection data and analysis; originally real estate, construction and mining customers renting drone pilots.
problem: Inspecting solar farms, wind turbines and grid assets by hand is slow and costly; Zeitview captures aerial and robotic data with a pilot network and analyzes it with AI. DroneBase began as a marketplace to rent a drone and pilot.
business_model: Services and software priced per inspection and portfolio; originally a marketplace commission of about 15 percent per job
product_category: Asset inspection software and aerial data capture

founders.name: Dan Burton
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Marine infantry, Goldman Sachs and US Senate staff; TechCrunch 2015 calls him a former Marine infantry officer.

founders.name: Eli Tamanaha
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch April 2015 describes him as a developer who worked at Microsoft, Amazon and Netflix; the YC page lists only Burton.

competitors.name: Skycatch
competitors.what: B2B drone data services company that also supplied pilots for jobs
competitors.traction_then: Named alongside DroneBase as supplying a pilot for the job

competitors.name: Droners.io
competitors.what: Marketplace where users post jobs and pilots bid, taking a 10 percent cut

technical_complexity.rationale: A pilot marketplace with scheduling, payments and later imagery processing is standard engineering; the AI inspection analytics of later years raised difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: A pilot network and growing inspection datasets helped, but the early marketplace was easy to copy and drone hardware makers were close by.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: DJI became an investor in 2018 rather than a competitor; DroneBase later bought Precision XYZ, Heliolytics assets (2023) and Clearsight assets (2024).

market_need_then: In April 2015 DroneBase's CEO said the first competitor was non consumption, meaning businesses in real estate, construction and mining had never bought aerial imagery; consumer drones and new FAA commercial rules were opening the market.

branding.name_origin: Zeitview is described in coverage as meaning time view or view time, from the German word for time; SiliconANGLE says the company meant view time, tied to near real time insights.
branding.domain_note: DroneBase used dronebase.com; the company now operates on zeitview.com and blog.zeitview.com redirects there.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and technical, framed around asset intelligence for energy and critical infrastructure

rebrands.why: The company says it rebranded to reflect an expanded mission beyond drone operations, since the DroneBase name limited it to drones

branding.community_and_virality: A global pilot network with a Become a Pilot sign up; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: DroneBase was well known in commercial drone circles and covered by TechCrunch, but the brand was changed because it limited the company's positioning.

pivots.from: DroneBase, a drone pilot marketplace and drone data services company
pivots.to: Zeitview, inspection software for renewable energy and infrastructure with multi sensor data capture
pivots.why: Expand beyond drones and focus on energy and infrastructure inspection; the shift toward solar and wind was reinforced by the Precision XYZ and Heliolytics acquisitions

outcome_analysis: DroneBase started as a drone pilot marketplace in 2015, raised from Union Square Ventures, then a Series A in 2016 and a 12M Series B in 2018, and pivoted toward enterprise inspection for renewable energy. In February 2023 it rebranded as Zeitview with a 55M tranche led by Valor taking reported total funding to 114M, and it kept acquiring assets such as Heliolytics and Clearsight, so it is a growing independent company.
notes: Totals conflict: TechCrunch 2023 gives 114M total, aggregators range 114M to 300M and mention a Series C (12.5M, 2021) and a 2025 round; those are single aggregator items and not recorded. The Series A 6.8M in mid 2016 is from a Crunchbase News snippet not opened. The Series B details come from a Business Wire headline and snippets; press release page not opened. Competitor sources are TNW dated September 2015, about six months after the Winter 2015 batch, noted here. Founding year 2014 per TechCrunch 2023 quote. Acquisitions of Precision XYZ, Heliolytics assets (2023) and Clearsight assets (July 2024) are from search snippets. No layoffs found.
